format.points_carry: full in the championship and relegation groups, half in the Europe play-offs

stages.name: championship_playoffs
stages.note: title and European places; 32 games, points carried in full

stages.name: europe_playoffs
stages.note: places 5-8; enter with half their regular-season points; only matters if the cup winner is already in the top four

stages.name: relegation_playouts
stages.note: places 9-14; decides the two relegated clubs

playoff.note: Relegation play-outs: the bottom six play each other twice (10 games) and the last two are relegated.

boundaries.note: Super League 2 promotes its top two directly, no play-off. Super League 1 decides both relegation places in the bottom-six play-outs, not by the regular-season table.

conflicts.real: one group of 16 in 2026-27, but two groups (North/South) in 2025-26
conflicts.note: The single group is new: the 2025-26 edition was split into a north and a south group, each with its own champion (Iraklis and Kalamata both went up). The reduction to 16 clubs in one group also removed the promotion play-offs and relegation play-outs.

notes: Super League 1 is 14 clubs: 26-round double round robin, then three separate second phases - championship play-offs (top 4, 6 games, points carried in full), Europe play-offs (5th-8th, 6 games, entering with half their points) and relegation play-outs (bottom 6, 10 games). Super League 2 is 16 clubs, 30 rounds, top two promoted, bottom four relegated to Gamma Ethniki (level 3, not in our rows) - no play-offs in either direction. Reserve sides (PAOK B, Asteras Tripolis B, Olympiacos B) are eligible for relegation but not for promotion, so a top-two finish by a B team does not open an extra promotion place. Unverified detail: whether the relegation play-outs carry regular-season points in full; if they do not, the two relegated clubs are decided inside the play-out group alone.
